node.statement: F2 MULTIPLICATIVE FLATNESS OF THE SIGN FIELD (2026-07-10, campaign cycle 91): the parity has NO character formula — pseudorandom in BOTH Fourier bases. Setup: by twisted-orbit invariance (sat 19) every generic j=2 frequency orbit has representative c = (1, a), so the sign field is a one-variable arithmetic function eps(a) on F_q^x. The full-group closed form (N(y) = 1 + chi_2(disc) fiber count turns the period product into a quadratic-character-twisted log-sum) suggested eps might be character-expressible — the theory-favored E2 shortcut. MEASURED at 6 exact rows (q = 97..577; full multiplicative-character spectrum via discrete-log FFT): max nontrivial character weight = 2.5-3.4 vs random +-1 baseline sqrt(2 ln(q-1)) = 3.0-3.6 — AT OR BELOW RANDOM at every row; explicit quadratic-character correlation 0.6-2.4 (negligible); top-character orders scattered (16/14/32/128/16/48 — no consistent low-order family). VERDICT: eps(a) carries no multiplicative structure; with satellite 23 (additive flatness) the sign field is spectrally pseudorandom in every available Fourier basis — it admits NO spectral description. CONSEQUENCE for the lane map: E2's character-shortcut is CLOSED; E2 survives only as exact Dedekind-type reciprocity for the carry integer K (identity theory, not spectral theory); E1 (Ehrhart mod-2 lattice parity) is the PRIMARY surviving lane. The sign quantization theorem's object is as hard as its coordinates are elementary — the campaign's honest reading: the parity field behaves like a perfect pseudorandom sign in every tested structure EXCEPT its exact lattice definition, which is where any proof must now live. Verifier: inline in campaign log #103 (local, small). Twenty-sixth satellite. COMPONENT ADDENDUM (cycle 92, E1 first contact): the parity COMPONENTS are individually pseudorandom too — over orbit reps at the same 6 rows, P(K odd) = 0.46-0.52 and P(U odd) = 0.40-0.55 (balanced), corr((-1)^K, (-1)^U) = -0.08..+0.17 (weak, sign-inconsistent), and the multiplicative spectra of (-1)^K and (-1)^U are SEPARATELY flat (max weights 1.9-3.1, all below the random baseline 3.0-3.6). No reduction of eps to a simpler single coordinate exists; the E1 lattice attack must handle the joint pair (K, U) as Ehrhart-type counts, not either alone.
